about.label: // ABOUT
about.heading: About Me
paragraphs: I'm Felix, a developer and designer driven by a passion for crafting seamless, aesthetically refined digital experiences. I care deeply about the details: clean interfaces, fluid interactions, and code that's built to last.
Currently pursuing a Computer Science degree at UBC's Okanagan campus, I bring a strong foundation in software engineering, AI, and cybersecurity to every project I take on.

I've been programming for over a decade, from my humble beginnings on Scratch and haven't looked back: from performant React and Next.js apps to machine learning and MCP orchestration, I'm always pushing what I can create and give back to the community.

I believe great technology should feel seemless: intuitive, fast, and purposeful. That philosophy drives everything I build, whether it's a client website, an open-source tool, or a personal experiment.

nputella.title: NPUtella
nputella.overview: Local NPU-powered speech-to-text for Snapdragon Windows PCs. Hold Ctrl+Win, speak, release — your words are transcribed offline and pasted instantly. Supports English, French, and bilingual dictation with no cloud dependency, zero latency, and total privacy. Built as a native Rust application using ONNX Runtime with Qualcomm's QNN Execution Provider to run Whisper directly on the NPU.

techStack.name: Rust
techStack.reason: Native Windows app with direct hardware access and zero startup latency

techStack.name: ONNX Runtime + QNN
techStack.reason: Routes Whisper inference to Qualcomm's NPU in FP16 burst mode

techStack.name: Whisper Base
techStack.reason: Multilingual speech recognition model, exported via Qualcomm AI Hub

techStack.name: WiX Toolset
techStack.reason: Standalone MSI installer — no dependencies on end-user machines

challenges: Getting Whisper to run on Qualcomm's NPU required ONNX model export through Qualcomm AI Hub with device-specific tensor layouts and context binaries.
Rewrote the entire app from Python to native Rust to eliminate startup latency and enable direct cpal audio capture and SendInput paste.
Built a borderless always-on-top overlay that stays visible across all apps while remaining unobtrusive — with recording, transcribing, and error states.
Implemented local post-processing for bilingual punctuation, code formatting, dictionary expansion, and snippet triggers — all without a network call.

paste-relay.title: Paste Relay
paste-relay.overview: Paste text or drop a file (up to 5 GB) on one device and pick it up on another within 5 minutes, then it's gone for good. The frontend lives at felixegan.me/paste; the backend runs on my home server behind a Cloudflare Tunnel with no open inbound ports. Accounts only exist through admin-issued invites, login is a drawn pattern grid, and every item is encrypted with a key derived from its own 4-digit PIN, which the server never stores.

techStack.name: Node.js + Express
techStack.reason: Streaming API for chunked uploads, range downloads and rate-limited auth routes

techStack.name: scrypt + AES-256-GCM
techStack.reason: Per-item key from PIN + salt + server pepper; content is never on disk in plaintext

techStack.name: ClamAV
techStack.reason: Self-hosted malware scan on every upload before it can be downloaded

techStack.name: Docker Compose
techStack.reason: Relay, scanner, admin dashboard and a least-privilege Docker socket proxy on separate networks

techStack.name: Cloudflare Tunnel + Turnstile
techStack.reason: Public exposure without open ports, plus bot protection on login

challenges: Streaming 5 GB through GCM: uploads are 16 MB chunks sent 8 at a time and written out of order at their byte offset, with a range tracker that refuses to finalize a file until every byte has arrived.
GCM only checks its auth tag at the end of a streaming decrypt, so wrong-PIN detection for files moved into the download route, including treating an aborted download as a failed attempt.
Making the PIN both the item's address and its key meant moving brute-force protection to per-account and per-IP counters, and returning 'not found' and 'wrong PIN' identically.
Network-segmented the internet-facing container away from the admin dashboard, which reads container uptime through a restricted socket proxy on its own network.

theta-health-check.title: Theta Health Check + AI Approval Gate
theta-health-check.overview: Once a day my home server audits itself (services, containers, network peers, disk) and DMs me the findings on Discord. If it suggests a fix, an AI agent can only act on it after two separate human approvals: one for the idea, one for the concrete plan. Even then, the agent only runs if the plan matches an explicitly enabled scope. Everything fails closed.

techStack.name: Python (stdlib only)
techStack.reason: No dependencies to break on a small always-on box: sqlite3, fcntl, hmac, concurrent.futures

techStack.name: SQLite ledger
techStack.reason: Durable de-duplication so a suggestion fires once and only returns if the issue clears and comes back

techStack.name: systemd template units
techStack.reason: One bounded approval listener and one implementation run per audit, each with its own lifetime

techStack.name: Discord components
techStack.reason: Approve / deny buttons where I already get notifications

challenges: Built the approval workflow as a pure, network-free state machine so every transition (pending, queued, running, denied, timed out) is unit-tested.
Handled the 'the message may have been sent' case explicitly so a retry never double-sends an approval request.
Kept only redacted, typed snapshots of probe output, with identifiers HMAC-aliased, so the audit history is safe to hand to an agent.
Capped agent runs by turns and wall time and archived a recap of every run, so an approved fix is still bounded and reviewable.

cloudsource.title: CloudSource
cloudsource.overview: A globe-first AI travel planner built during a hackathon with my girlfriend. The entire experience orbits around a 3D Cesium globe — panels for flights, culture, hotels, budget, notes, and an AI assistant called Nimbus slide into view as you explore destinations. AI-generated trip plans give you a structured starting point, and shared client-side state keeps everything in sync as you plan.

techStack.name: Cesium

techStack.name: Google AI

techStack.name: Framer Motion

challenges: Integrating a full 3D Cesium globe into a multi-panel React app under hackathon time pressure.
Keeping trip state synchronized across globe navigation, flight search, budget tracking, and AI chat — all in shared client-side state.
Building the AI trip generator to return structured, Zod-validated JSON that the planning flow could consume without manual parsing.

aura.title: AURA — Unity Robot Analysis
aura.overview: Final robotics project exploring autonomous robot training through reinforcement learning in Unity. Robots learn to navigate and perform tasks in simulated environments using ML-Agents, with reward-driven behavior shaping their decisions over thousands of training iterations. A full Python analysis pipeline handles model mutation, performance parsing, and success-rate visualization.

techStack.reason: Simulated 3D environments for training and testing robot behaviors

techStack.name: ML-Agents
techStack.reason: Unity's reinforcement learning toolkit for training autonomous agents

techStack.name: Python
techStack.reason: Model mutation, training data parsing, and performance visualization

techStack.name: Reinforcement Learning
techStack.reason: Reward-shaped behavior — agents improve through trial and error, not hardcoded rules

challenges: Designing reward functions that produce meaningful robot behaviors without over-fitting to exploitable shortcuts.
Iterating on model mutations across multiple generations to evolve better-performing agents — visible in the project's mutation pipeline.
Parsing and visualizing training data to identify which models actually learned versus which got lucky in specific scenarios.
Bridging Unity's C# simulation environment with Python analysis scripts for a seamless train-evaluate-mutate loop.

The portfolio side runs a real-time Three.js starfield that reacts to scroll and mouse, a hidden terminal easter egg, and content driven from one JSON file. The studio side has case studies, a blog, testimonials, and two lead paths: a discovery-call form that lands in a self-hosted CRM and a quote form backed by Supabase.

Running a personal portfolio and a client-facing business site from one codebase without either feeling bolted on.
Sending form leads into a CRM on my home server without ever exposing its API key to the browser.
Per-route SEO, a sitemap and machine-readable site maps for a client-rendered React app.

pluto-phone.title: Pluto Phone Gateway
pluto-phone.overview: A phone line for my assistant, Pluto. You call a Twilio number, pass an allowlist and a DTMF PIN, and then talk to Pluto live. It takes a voicemail-style message, records it, summarizes it and sends the summary to me by MMS, with SMS as a fallback. Built and tested; the service is currently paused.

Validates Twilio signatures on both webhooks and on the WebSocket handshake.
Recording links are HMAC-signed, expire after 5 minutes, and recordings are deleted after delivery.
Bridging telephony audio frames and a realtime model session without audible lag.

hermes-agent.title: Hermes Agent Deployment + Upstream Fixes
hermes-agent.overview: I run the open-source Hermes Agent as my personal assistant, Pluto: a Discord gateway, a web dashboard behind Caddy, MCP servers, and scheduled jobs like a daily email-drafting run. It's also the notification backbone for my server tooling. Running it daily surfaced real bugs, so I wrote 7 resilience patches (+1,171 lines across 15 files) against the upstream project.

techStack.reason: The agent framework and all patches

techStack.name: Caddy
techStack.reason: Reverse proxy for the dashboard, normalizing the Host header

techStack.reason: Plugs external tools into the agent

The stale-timeout ladder keeps scaling past 100k-token contexts instead of flattening.
The doctor command never reports an audit that couldn't run as one that passed.
'Too many pending requests' is classified as a rate limit, and a terminal failed or cancelled model response is treated as invalid instead of success.

ops-mcp.title: Field Ops MCP Server
ops-mcp.overview: A remote Model Context Protocol server that connects Claude to a field-services company's job, lead and estimate platform and its sales-call CRM. It exposes 40+ tools: lookups, schema introspection, a prioritized 7-day production brief, crew workload and overload flags, geographic job clustering with route-risk flags, sales-call QA, and sales-to-ops handoffs. Used daily as a claude.ai connector.

techStack.reason: Typed tool definitions over both stdio and Streamable HTTP

techStack.name: Express 5
techStack.reason: HTTP transport plus a built-in OAuth 2.1 authorization server

techStack.name: GraphQL

techStack.name: Geocoding + cache
techStack.reason: Location clustering with a 180-day geocode cache

Token-budget aware by default: list tools scan several pages but cap backend pages and returned rows, and raw nested data is opt-in.
Implemented the full OAuth flow (metadata, dynamic client registration, authorize, token, refresh, revoke) so it connects through the standard browser flow.
One JSON envelope and named error codes across all tools, so the model can recover from auth expiry or missing approvals on its own.

lead-intake-crm.title: Lead Intake → Self-hosted CRM
lead-intake-crm.overview: The production lead pipeline for my studio. The discovery-call form on /studio posts to a Vercel function that validates it, then goes through a Cloudflare Tunnel to a restricted proxy on my home server, which writes into a self-hosted Twenty CRM. The handler finds or creates the company and person, opens an opportunity, and attaches the call details as a note.

techStack.reason: Zero-dependency intake proxy that only allows specific methods on specific collections

techStack.name: Cloudflare Tunnel
techStack.reason: Reaches the home server without opening inbound ports

Allow-list proxy: 5 collections, fixed methods, 20 KB body cap.
Tuned upstream timeouts after real CRM writes turned out slower than a serverless default allows.
Log rotation, backups and a keep-alive runbook so it survives being run by one person.

sf-study-tools.title: SF Study Tools
sf-study-tools.overview: A study site for Dawson College's SF1 to SF3 programming courses, shared with classmates for finals. It has word jumbles, flashcards, ConcepTests, 'Stack or Queue?', Pandas/Matplotlib drills, Spot-the-Bug, 'Final Boss' problems, an OOP inheritance diagram, a step-by-step code animator, a Big-O calculator, an in-browser Python terminal with file I/O, and a concept map. Progress is saved locally.

techStack.reason: Consistent styling across very different exercise types

techStack.name: In-browser Python
techStack.reason: Run and debug code without installing anything

Fitting a dozen content types (flashcards, drills, animators, a terminal) into one coherent flow.
Saving progress locally so students don't lose their place when they close the tab.

agentrun.title: agentrun: 4-Layer Coding-Agent Fallback
agentrun.overview: An orchestrator that runs a coding task through a priority chain of separate agent CLIs, each on its own login and billing: Codex CLI, then Claude Code (subscription only, gated below a usage cap so it never spends API credits), then Google's Antigravity CLI on the free tier, then Codex on a local Ollama model as the offline last resort.

techStack.name: Python
techStack.reason: Ordering, usage gating, timeouts and fall-through decisions

techStack.name: Bash
techStack.reason: Thin CLI wrapper installed on the path

techStack.name: Ollama
techStack.reason: Local models for the offline layer

challenges: The orchestrator only decides order and when to fall through; each layer stays a real, unmodified CLI.
`agentrun local-verify` pulls a model, loads it and runs a memory-guarded smoke test before enabling it, so a slow local model can't take down the shared server.
Documented which small local models failed on 3.7 GB of RAM so the next attempt starts from real data.

claude-rc.title: claude-rc
claude-rc.overview: Keeps my home server reachable from the Claude app's Code tab around the clock. A launcher with preflight checks and crash-loop backoff, an updater that stages, smoke-tests and rolls back, and a watchdog that runs a self-test every 15 minutes and messages me on Discord when something is wrong.

techStack.name: Bash
techStack.reason: Launcher, updater and watchdog scripts

techStack.name: Python
techStack.reason: Safe config edits while holding the app's own lock

techStack.name: systemd timers
techStack.reason: Supervision, scheduled updates and the watchdog

challenges: Update pipeline: stage, smoke test, wait for 60 idle minutes, switch, verify, roll back if needed, prune. Forward-only, with a denylist of bad versions.
Versioned installs behind a symlink so a rollback is one atomic switch.
A session can't restart its own service without killing itself, so restarts are handed off through a detached systemd-run.
The watchdog alerts on sustained failure, crash loops, rollbacks, and a login expiring within 3 days.

instagram-analysis.title: Instagram Export Analysis
instagram-analysis.overview: A pipeline that processes a full Instagram data export (200k+ records across six years) entirely on my own machine. It parses Meta's HTML export into one structured dataset, transcribes audio and video, captions and tags images, builds per-thread statistics and a writing-style profile, and turns it all into a social knowledge graph with detected communities and an interactive view. Only the methods are shown here; the data is private.

techStack.name: BLIP
techStack.reason: Local image captioning

techStack.name: CLIP
techStack.reason: Zero-shot image tagging without training a classifier

techStack.name: Local transcription
techStack.reason: Speech-to-text for thousands of clips without sending audio anywhere

techStack.name: Graph clustering
techStack.reason: Community detection over the social graph, exported as GraphML/JSON

challenges: A deterministic parser for Meta's HTML export, which isn't designed to be machine-read.
Resumable, checkpointed stages with progress and ETA watchers so the job could run unattended on a 3.7 GB RAM box.
A writing-style profile (message length, bursts, openers, verbal tics) meant to ground an assistant that writes like me.

theta.title: Theta Home Server Platform
theta.overview: The infrastructure under most of these projects: a single Ubuntu server with 3.7 GB of RAM that reliably hosts production services for my studio and my personal AI stack. Public services go out through Cloudflare Tunnels and private ones through Tailscale, so nothing listens on an open port.

techStack.name: Tailscale
techStack.reason: Private access, MagicDNS, and Funnel for the one endpoint that needs it

techStack.reason: Reverse proxy and routing for the agent and phone services

Fitting a CRM, an AI agent, a file relay and a malware scanner onto 3.7 GB of RAM.
Ops discipline for a one-person setup: runbooks, log-rotation overrides, and a checksummed archive before any cleanup.

pluto.title: PLUTO AI Assistant
pluto.overview: Personal & Logical Utility Task Organizer — a fully local, open-source AI assistant built with privacy at its core. PLUTO handles personal tasks, reminders, and information retrieval without sending a single byte to external servers. Designed as an extensible framework for anyone who wants an AI assistant they actually own.

techStack.reason: Rapid prototyping and access to the NLP/AI ecosystem

techStack.name: NLP Libraries

instagram-vault.title: Pluto Instagram Vault
instagram-vault.overview: When I share a post or reel to a specific Instagram DM, a webhook turns it into a Markdown note in an Obsidian vault, with YAML frontmatter and wikilinks to topic and account hub notes. My assistant can then search it later for travel, food, home or software ideas. The vault is plain files, so the agent needs no Obsidian plugin.

Search works by meaning: looking for 'burgundy sneakers' finds a note about 'red shoes'. Includes memory stats and trends in a space-themed, mobile-friendly UI.

onewheel-battery.title: Onewheel Battery Curve Fit
onewheel-battery.overview: Fits the pack-voltage to state-of-charge curve for an electric skateboard. For each polynomial degree it finds the true minimax error with linear programming (the exact global optimum, not hill-climbing), then finds the fewest significant figures the coefficients can be hardcoded at without meaningfully increasing that error.

challenges: Sweeping degree against printed precision to find the smallest formula that is still accurate.
